bands.name: MC5
bands.disambiguation: Detroit proto-punk band, the Motor City Five
bands.description: Louder and more political than anything else in 1968: a band managed by the White Panther Party, playing at a volume rock had not used before. Punk's grandparents.
bands.label: Elektra

bands.name: The Stooges
bands.disambiguation: Iggy Pop's band, originally The Psychedelic Stooges
bands.description: Three chords, one riff repeated until it hurts, and a singer who threw himself into the crowd. Everything punk would later take for granted was already here.
bands.label: Elektra

bands.name: Death
bands.disambiguation: Detroit proto-punk trio of the Hackney brothers, not the death metal band
bands.description: Three Black brothers playing punk in Detroit before the word existed. Labels wanted them to change the name; they refused, and the tapes sat in an attic for thirty years.
bands.label: Drag City

bands.name: New York Dolls
bands.disambiguation: American glam punk band from Manhattan
bands.description: Platform heels, lipstick and songs that barely held together. Malcolm McLaren managed them briefly, then went home to London and built the Sex Pistols out of what he had learned.
bands.label: Mercury

bands.name: Suicide
bands.disambiguation: New York synth-punk duo
bands.description: A drum machine, one cheap keyboard and a singer screaming into the feedback. They proved punk never needed a guitar, and got bottles thrown at them for ten years.
bands.label: Red Star

bands.name: Television
bands.disambiguation: CBGB band led by Tom Verlaine
bands.description: The band that talked CBGB into booking rock groups, which is why the scene happened there at all. Ten-minute guitar interplay: punk in attitude, never in form.
bands.label: Elektra

bands.name: Ramones
bands.disambiguation: American punk rock band from Queens
bands.description: Four men in leather jackets, the same surname and none of them brothers. Two-minute songs at full speed: the template every punk band since has either copied or reacted against.
bands.label: Sire

bands.name: Sex Pistols
bands.disambiguation: English punk rock band managed by Malcolm McLaren

albums.title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols

bands.description: One album, two and a half years, and a hole in British culture that never closed. Jamie Reid's ransom-note sleeves did as much damage as the songs.
bands.label: Virgin

bands.name: The Damned
bands.disambiguation: First UK punk band to release a single and an album
bands.description: New Rose beat the Pistols to the shops by five weeks, making them the first UK punk single. They then spent forty years refusing to stay punk, inventing goth on the way.
bands.label: Stiff

bands.name: The Clash
bands.disambiguation: English punk rock band, the only band that mattered
bands.description: The band that refused punk's three-chord rule and pulled reggae, dub, rockabilly and hip-hop into it. London Calling is a punk record only in attitude.
bands.label: CBS

bands.name: Buzzcocks
bands.disambiguation: Manchester punk band, pioneers of the self-released EP

albums.title: Another Music in a Different Kitchen

bands.description: They put out Spiral Scratch themselves in 1977 and accidentally invented the independent record label. Then they wrote love songs, which in punk was the real provocation.
bands.label: New Hormones

bands.name: Siouxsie and the Banshees
bands.disambiguation: English post-punk band from the Bromley Contingent
bands.description: Their first gig was twenty minutes of the Lord's Prayer over noise, with no songs written. Four years later they were the blueprint for goth.
bands.label: Polydor

bands.name: Joy Division
bands.disambiguation: Manchester post-punk band, formerly Warsaw
bands.description: Four Manchester teenagers who saw the Sex Pistols at the Lesser Free Trade Hall and went home to form a band. They played punk slowly, and post-punk existed.
bands.label: Factory

bands.name: Black Flag
bands.disambiguation: American hardcore band founded by Greg Ginn, originally Panic
bands.description: They built the American touring circuit from nothing, playing halls no promoter would book, and founded SST to release themselves. Raymond Pettibon's four bars became punk's most tattooed logo.
bands.label: SST

bands.name: Bad Brains
bands.disambiguation: All-Black hardcore band from Washington D.C., formerly a jazz fusion group
bands.description: Jazz musicians who heard punk and played it faster than anyone thought possible, then stopped mid-set for a dub reggae song. Banned from most D.C. venues, which is how the city got its own scene.
bands.label: ROIR

bands.name: Crass
bands.disambiguation: English anarcho-punk collective based at Dial House
bands.description: A commune that printed its own records with the price stamped on the sleeve so no shop could overcharge. They took punk's politics literally and made everyone else look like a pose.
bands.label: Crass Records

bands.name: Discharge
bands.disambiguation: English hardcore band whose drum pattern became the d-beat

albums.title: Hear Nothing See Nothing Say Nothing

bands.description: Lyrics stripped to slogans shouted over one relentless drum pattern. That pattern is now called the d-beat and has its own genre, which few bands can claim.
bands.label: Clay

bands.name: The Misfits
bands.disambiguation: American horror punk band founded by Glenn Danzig
bands.description: B-movie monsters, devilocks and a skull logo more famous than any of the songs. They invented horror punk and sold more shirts after splitting up than records before.
bands.label: Plan 9

bands.name: Descendents
bands.disambiguation: American pop punk band, Milo on the sleeves

albums.title: I Don't Want to Grow Up

bands.description: Hardcore speed with melodies, and songs about coffee, food and being rejected. Their singer left to get a PhD in biochemistry, which is the most Descendents fact available.
bands.label: SST

bands.name: Public Image Ltd
bands.disambiguation: John Lydon's band after the Sex Pistols, PiL
bands.description: Lydon's answer to being asked to repeat himself: dub bass, scraped guitar and no choruses. Metal Box came in a film canister because a sleeve would have been too normal.
bands.label: Virgin

bands.name: Amebix
bands.disambiguation: English band credited with inventing crust punk
bands.description: Anarcho-punk slowed to a crawl and dragged through Motorhead and Black Sabbath. The word crust comes from one of their songs, and the whole genre followed.
bands.label: Alternative Tentacles

bands.name: Dead Kennedys
bands.disambiguation: American hardcore band fronted by Jello Biafra until 1986
bands.description: Satire sharp enough to be mistaken for the thing it attacked, over surf guitar played at hardcore speed. An obscenity trial over a poster in Frankenchrist nearly destroyed them.
bands.label: Alternative Tentacles

bands.name: Cockney Rejects
bands.disambiguation: East London Oi! band
bands.description: Football terraces turned into a chorus, sung by teenagers from the docks. Oi! was meant to be punk for the working class punk claimed to be about, and they meant it.
bands.label: EMI

bands.name: GBH
bands.disambiguation: Birmingham hardcore punk band, formerly Charged GBH
bands.description: Studded leather, spiked hair and riffs borrowed from metal without admitting it. With Discharge and the Exploited, they are the three names UK82 is built on.
bands.label: Clay

bands.name: Social Distortion
bands.disambiguation: Orange County punk band led by Mike Ness
bands.description: Orange County hardcore that drifted into Johnny Cash territory and never came back. Tattoos, rockabilly chords and songs about prison and regret.
bands.label: Epitaph

bands.name: The Exploited
bands.disambiguation: Scottish punk band fronted by Wattie Buchan
bands.description: The band that put Punks Not Dead on a million jacket backs, then spent the eighties getting faster and heavier until hardcore and thrash met in the middle.
bands.label: Secret

bands.name: The Business
bands.disambiguation: English Oi! band from South London
bands.description: Oi! that went out of its way to say the scene was not for racists, at a time when saying so got you threatened. Pub-singalong choruses with a picket line behind them.
bands.label: Secret

bands.name: Bad Religion
bands.disambiguation: Los Angeles melodic hardcore band, the crossbuster logo

albums.title: How Could Hell Be Any Worse?

bands.description: Three-part vocal harmonies, a PhD-level vocabulary and the guitarist who founded Epitaph, the label that later funded half of nineties punk.
bands.label: Epitaph

bands.name: Minor Threat
bands.disambiguation: D.C. hardcore band that named straight edge
bands.description: Three years, about thirty minutes of music, and an entire subculture. A forty-six second song called Straight Edge gave a name to not drinking, which MacKaye spent decades insisting was never meant as a rule.
bands.label: Dischord

bands.name: Minutemen
bands.disambiguation: California trio, we jam econo

albums.title: What Makes a Man Start Fires?

bands.description: Forty-three songs on a double album, most under ninety seconds, built from funk, jazz and politics. We jam econo was a philosophy, not a slogan. It ended when D. Boon died in a van crash.
bands.label: SST

bands.name: Suicidal Tendencies
bands.disambiguation: Venice crossover band led by Mike Muir

albums.title: How Will I Laugh Tomorrow When I Can't Even Smile Today

bands.description: Institutionalized put skate punk on MTV in 1983. Hardcore kids called them metal and metal kids called them punk, which is roughly the definition of crossover.
bands.label: Frontier

bands.name: Anti-Cimex
bands.disambiguation: Swedish d-beat band, founders of kangpunk
bands.description: They took Discharge's beat, played it with more distortion than the tape could hold, and created the Swedish sound that crust and metal are still copying.
bands.label: Distortion

bands.name: Siege
bands.disambiguation: Massachusetts band whose 1984 demo predates powerviolence
bands.description: Six songs on a demo almost nobody heard at the time, faster than anything else in 1984. Napalm Death and every powerviolence band afterwards cite it as the starting point.
bands.label: Deep Six

bands.name: The Stalin
bands.disambiguation: Japanese punk band led by Michiro Endo
bands.description: The band that made Japanese punk notorious, as much for what was thrown at the audience as for the songs. Japan's hardcore scene starts here.
bands.label: Tokuma

bands.name: G.I.S.M.
bands.disambiguation: Japanese hardcore band fronted by Sakevi Yokoyama
bands.description: Hardcore welded to heavy metal guitar solos years before crossover was a word, with artwork and a live reputation that kept them half-legendary and half-unreleasable.
bands.label: Dogma

bands.name: Ratos de Porao
bands.disambiguation: Brazilian hardcore band, RxDxPx
bands.description: Brazil's hardcore institution: dictatorship-era fury that kept going for forty years and turned into the loudest crossover band in South America.
bands.label: Roadrunner

bands.name: Napalm Death
bands.disambiguation: English grindcore band, Scum and You Suffer
bands.description: Anarcho-punk accelerated past the point of structure. You Suffer lasts about one second and holds the record for the shortest song ever recorded, which tells you the whole project.
bands.label: Earache

bands.name: D.R.I.
bands.disambiguation: Dirty Rotten Imbeciles, the dancing skater logo
bands.description: Twenty-two songs in eighteen minutes on their first record, then an album literally called Crossover that named a genre. The dancing skater stencil is on more battle jackets than most logos.
bands.label: Metal Blade

bands.name: NOFX
bands.disambiguation: Los Angeles skate punk band, Fat Wreck Chords

albums.title: So Long and Thanks for All the Shoes

bands.description: Forty years without ever signing to a major label, and a singer who ran Fat Wreck Chords on the side. They played their last shows in 2024 and stopped on their own terms.
bands.label: Fat Wreck Chords

bands.name: Rites of Spring
bands.disambiguation: D.C. band of the Revolution Summer, the first called emo
bands.description: About fifteen shows in two years. They turned hardcore's anger inward and got called emocore for it, a label the band never wanted and could not escape.
bands.label: Dischord

bands.name: Operation Ivy
bands.disambiguation: Berkeley ska punk band of the Gilman Street scene
bands.description: Two years, one album, and the sound every nineties ska punk band started from. They split the week Energy came out, and two of them went on to form Rancid.
bands.label: Lookout!

bands.name: Fugazi
bands.disambiguation: D.C. post-hardcore band on Dischord
bands.description: Five dollar shows, ten dollar records, no merchandise and no major labels, for fifteen years. The proof that punk's ethics could survive being successful.
bands.label: Dischord

bands.name: Doom
bands.disambiguation: English crust punk band from Birmingham
bands.description: The Birmingham end of crust: Discharge's beat, Amebix's filth and lyric sheets with their sources cited. Police Bastard is still the genre's standard cover version.
bands.label: Peaceville

bands.name: Cap'n Jazz
bands.disambiguation: Chicago emo band of the Kinsella brothers
bands.description: Teenagers playing twinkling guitar lines under a singer who yelped rather than sang. Nobody bought it at the time; every midwest emo band since has taken notes.
bands.label: Man with Gun

bands.name: Bikini Kill
bands.disambiguation: Olympia band at the centre of riot grrrl
bands.description: Girls to the front was an instruction given from the stage, not a slogan. They wrote the zines, booked the shows and made riot grrrl a movement rather than a sound.
bands.label: Kill Rock Stars

bands.name: Converge
bands.disambiguation: Massachusetts metalcore band, Jane Doe
bands.description: Hardcore pulled apart and reassembled wrong: time signatures that trip, a guitarist who became one of the genre's defining producers, and Jane Doe's face on a thousand shirts.
bands.label: Deathwish

bands.name: Rancid
bands.disambiguation: Berkeley street punk band formed out of Operation Ivy
bands.description: The band that turned down a major label at the exact moment Green Day signed one. Mohawks, ska horns and the Clash's record collection.
bands.label: Epitaph

bands.name: Pansy Division
bands.disambiguation: San Francisco queercore band on Lookout!
bands.description: Pop punk with explicitly gay lyrics, opening Green Day's biggest tour in 1994 and playing it to arenas of teenagers who had never heard anything like it.
bands.label: Lookout!

bands.name: Refused
bands.disambiguation: Swedish hardcore band from Umea, The Shape of Punk to Come

albums.title: Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent
The Shape of Punk to Come

bands.description: They put electronics, jazz and a manifesto into a hardcore record, split up weeks after releasing it, and watched it become the most imitated album in the genre.
bands.themes: class politics, veganism, art as refusal
bands.label: Burning Heart

bands.name: Dropkick Murphys
bands.disambiguation: Boston celtic punk band
bands.description: Boston Oi! with bagpipes, union songs and a Woody Guthrie obsession. The one celtic punk band that filled arenas without losing the picket line.
bands.label: Hellcat

bands.name: The Pogues
bands.disambiguation: Anglo-Irish celtic punk band fronted by Shane MacGowan

albums.title: If I Should Fall from Grace with God

bands.description: Irish traditional music played with punk's speed and punk's self-destruction. MacGowan had been in a London punk band before deciding an accordion was more offensive.
bands.label: Stiff

bands.name: The Cramps
bands.disambiguation: CBGB band of Lux Interior and Poison Ivy
bands.description: Rockabilly records, horror films and no bass player. They invented psychobilly almost by accident while trying to sound like 1958 heard through a broken speaker.
bands.label: IRS

bands.name: Pennywise
bands.disambiguation: South Bay skate punk band on Epitaph
bands.description: Melodic hardcore from the same few streets as Black Flag and the Descendents. Bro Hymn became a funeral song for their own bass player, and then for half of punk.
bands.label: Epitaph

bands.name: Orchid
bands.disambiguation: Massachusetts screamo band on Ebullition
bands.description: Screamo at its most severe: thirty-second songs, critical theory on the sleeves and a singer who sounded like the tape was tearing. Five years, no compromises.
bands.label: Ebullition
